3. 130.30 ppm: Could be an aromatic hydrogen (Ar-H) or a double-bonded carbon (=CR2) (115-130 ppm).
4. 26.65 ppm: Likely corresponds to an alkyl carbon (R3C-, R2CH, RCH2) (25-50 ppm).
5. 22.80 ppm: Likely corresponds to an alkyl carbon (R3C-, R2CH, RCH2) (25-50 ppm).
6. 21.35 ppm: Likely corresponds to a methyl group (CH3-) (10-30 ppm).
7. 19.20 ppm: Likely corresponds to a methyl group (CH3-) (10-30 ppm).

Based on these interpretations, the unique carbon environments are:

- Carboxylic ester
- Aromatic or double-bonded carbon
- Aromatic or double-bonded carbon
- Alkyl carbon
- Methyl group
